title: Preflight propensity KPI checklist and staffflow notes
body:
Purpose and context:

This is a working preflight for the next hosted API microlaunch (soft beta) focused on improving user propensity to upgrade from free tier to paid. The doc blends a KPI tracker, low-friction operational checklist, and a minimal staffflow for the first 72h after traffic unfreeze. Not final — sketching thresholds and owners so engineering, product and ops can align on what to instrument and who to call.

Why "propensity" here?
- We want to treat the launch as an activation experiment: unit economics depend on not just raw requests but downstream conversion. Metrics must include both infra health (latency, error rate) and behavioral signals (click-to-upgrade rate, session length).

Core success criteria (beta):
- Service-level: 99.9% successful inference responses within target latency bucket for 90% of traffic during soft roll (see latency buckets below).
- Behavioral lift: ≥ 12% uplift in 7-day upgrade propensity for cohort exposed to new prompt templates vs control.
- Cost guardrail: incremental cost per new paying user <= $12 (inferred from token unit cost + infra overhead).

KPI tracker (primary):
- API success rate (p95) -> target >= 99.9%
- P95 latency (inference) -> target <= 1200ms for common sequences, <= 250ms for cached-prefix flows
- Token cost per request (avg) -> budget <= $0.008/request (hosted API baseline)
- 7-day upgrade propensity (cohort A) -> target >= 12% uplift vs cohort B
- Error budget burn rate -> keep < 2% of daily error budget during ramp
- Queue length (per-gpu) -> alert if > 20% sustained for 5m

KPI tracker (secondary / diagnostic):
- Cache hit rate (KV prefix) -> want >= 30% during peak for templated prompts
- Batch size distribution -> median batch size 6–12 tokens per GPU cycle
- Model fallback frequency -> < 0.5% of requests fall back to smaller model
- Re-rate limit events per minute -> < 10/min for rollout window

Thresholds and automated triggers (runbook hooks):
- If API success rate < 99.5% for 10 minutes -> page SRE on-call (pager duty)
- If p95 latency climbs above 2.0s for 5 minutes -> scale up Dedicated pool (if available) and open incident channel #prodops-launch
- If upgrade propensity delta (A vs B) negative at 24h -> pause feature experiment and revert prompt templates

Staffflow and primary contacts (first 72h):
- Launch commander: Maya Chen (product-ops) — overall go/no-go and comms
- Runtime lead: Ravi Patel (serving-runtime) — kernel selection, batch tuning, live model swaps
- SRE pager: on-call from SRE rotation (see roster) — incident routing and mitigation
- Data/metrics: Elena Gomez (applied-ml) — cohort extraction, propensity calc, data pipeline checks
- Customer comms: Samir Kaur (customer-success) — triage customer reports and coordinate beta invites

Shifted responsibilities (hand-offs):
- Preflight (T-48 to T-1): product-ops + runtime finalize batching/config recommended profiles
- Launch (T+0 to T+6h): SRE + runtime handle immediate infra, product-ops monitors KPI dashboard and behavioral signal
- Stabilize (T+6h to T+72h): applied-ml owns propensity analysis cadence (6h, 24h, 72h) and communicates gating recommendations

Immediate preflight checklist (T-48h -> T-0):
- [ ] Confirm canary routing policy (10% traffic -> 30% -> 60% over 3 steps) in Console. Owner: Maya
- [ ] Validate auto-scaling policy for dedicated pools (min nodes, hot spare) and pre-warm GPUs. Owner: Ravi
- [ ] Run smoke harness for templated prompt set (50 synthetic requests) and check cache hit rate > 20%. Owner: Ravi, Elena
- [ ] Instrument an experiment flag and conversion metric (upgrade flag) in metrics pipeline. Owner: Elena
- [ ] Prepare fallback model (quantized variant) and ensure compatibility with response format. Owner: Ravi
- [ ] Draft customer-facing beta note and FAQ for first 24h. Owner: Samir
- [ ] Confirm observability dashboard: token cost, per-route latency, cohort conversion. Owner: Maya
- [ ] Prepare throttling policy docs and service limits page for support. Owner: Samir

Launch day quick playbook (T+0 to T+6h):
- Step 0 — Unfreeze traffic to pre-set canary percentage. Notify #prodops-launch.
- Step 1 — Observe API success rate / p95 latency every 5 minutes for first 30 minutes, then 15-min cadence.
- Step 2 — Elena runs a quick cohort check at 6h to ensure metrics pipeline is ingesting upgrade signals correctly (smoke query + CSV snapshot).
- Step 3 — If queue length per GPU > 20% and latencies rising, execute scale-up recipe (auto-scale override to +25% capacity). Owner: SRE
- Step 4 — If error spike (5x baseline) or p95 > 2s sustained -> rollback canary to previous model variant and page incident lead.

Data artifacts to produce (immediately after launch):
- 6h snapshot CSV of: request_id, route, latency_ms, tokens, cache_hit, error_code, cohort_id, upgrade_flag
- 24h propensity report: baseline vs exposed cohort with lift, p-value, and unit-cost per conversion

Open questions / risks (to resolve pre-T-0):
- Can we guarantee prefix cache effectiveness for templated prompts? If not, expected latency and cost plan needs revision. (action: run wide template load-run — Ravi)
- Is the cohort attribution (who saw new prompts) robust to front-end retries and dedup? Need idempotency key logic. (action: Elena + FE squad)
- Model fallback throttling: is our routing layer correctly doing capacity-aware fallbacks or will it overload smaller models? (action: infra + runtime)

Lightweight experiments and guardrails to reduce blast radius:
- Feature gating: always gate creative prompt changes behind experiment flag with instant rollback toggle in Console.
- Gradual ramp with health checkpoints (canary to 10% -> 30% -> 60%) requiring manual approval at each step unless keys are green.
- Minute-resolution alerts for cache hit rate drops; if hit rate drops > 10% absolute, pause ramp and investigate.

Handy links and quick commands:
- Console canary control: /console/project/canaries -> preflight group "propensity-beta"
- Run smoke harness: gh actions -> ./scripts/smoke-propensity.sh --count 50
- Query metric: graphite.prod.p95_latency.route.propensity

Decision points and escalation ladder:
- At 6h: if API-level health OK and early propensity signal positive -> continue to 60% by 12h.
- At 24h: product-ops + applied-ml decide to expand to 100% or roll back based on 24h propensity and unit-cost.
- Escalation: any incident classified Sev1 -> SRE lead + Runtime lead + Product-ops commander on call immediately.

Notes to self / team reminders (informal):
- Keep message terse during first hour — we want signal, not commentary. Use #prodops-launch for status pings only.
- Elastic capacity arrangements (if Dedicated) have 30m spin-up — plan buffer for sudden surge.
- We will likely tune batching thresholds after first 6h by observing median batch size. Don’t pre-opt aggressively.

Appendix: quick KPI calculation example (text):
- If we saw 10k users in cohort A and 1.2k upgrades over 7 days -> propensity = 12%; baseline B had 10k and 1.05k -> 10.5% -> uplift = 14% relative. If average token cost during experiment = $0.004 per session and expected sessions per new payer = 30 -> cost per new paying user = 30 * 0.004 = $0.12 + infra overhead approximated at $3 => ~ $3.12 (well under $12 guardrail).

Next actions (short):
action_items: Ravi: run templated prompt load-run and share cache hit projections by 2024-11-18
Elena: wire upgrade_flag into metrics pipeline and validate end-to-end by 2024-11-20
Samir: draft beta FAQ and support triage playbook by 2024-11-19
Maya: finalize canary rollout schedule and send comms to stakeholders by 2024-11-21
